assessment: The frozen authored form passes the predeclared dated ENTRY-FACADE and characteristic tower SILHOUETTE review. It is not a four-façade, exact material, 1:1 landscape, navigation or survey pass. One upper side feature is visibly absent. No production parameters were fitted to these observers’ images.
scope: Souris East Historic Lighthouse on Knight Point, 134 Breakwater Street, Kings County. Geographic identity and four directional façade layouts are separate questions.
historicalControl: The first, different candidate separated the only door from the two windows. That architectural study failed; its 2012/2024 observations are already opened regression evidence, never counted as new tests. The former 2024 town aerial does not confirm the tower façade. All Jarvis October 2015 views are one artist reference session, not independent witnesses.

independentPhotoSessions.rights: All rights reserved. Observed normal public display; no source image, frame, crop or texture is distributed.
independentPhotoSessions.finding: An oblique view shows the three-opening entrance stack on one face and a separate high sash on the adjacent wall to its image-left. The white taper, red projecting bracketed gallery with open rails, clear upper lantern over a red base and rounded cap read distinctly. Strong contrast in a dramatic sky cannot calibrate material or paint.

independentPhotoSessions.rights: All rights reserved. Observed normal public display only; do not reuse imagery.
independentPhotoSessions.finding: The sea-side view directly resolves the central gabled entrance, centrally aligned gabled middle sash and straight-capped upper sash under the gallery. The grassy foreground masks the lower entrance. On the opposite visible flank to image-right a narrow red upper opening/trim is discernible under the gallery; panes do not resolve at this grazing angle.

boundedPass: In the ordinary locked 900×600 entrance render, a true gabled door, gabled middle opening and plain upper opening are present on the same original mesh face. The two separate field sessions corroborate their order and recognizable tower mass, palette and gallery/lantern silhouette. The preregistered opposing digital view independently renders two gabled openings without a door; that is a fact about the game, not a photographic verification of that rear façade.
knownFailure: The emitted source has a high-only windowed flank 0 and a wholly blank flank 2 next to the entrance 3. The two new photos view opposite flanks of that same entrance: 2018 resolves a high window on one, 2022 shows a narrow upper red-trimmed feature on the other. The already-opened 2012 beach photo separately resolves that second upper aperture more clearly. The second upper side feature is OMITTED in this model. A whole-tower azimuth change does not restore it.
otherLimits: No independent held view here directly resolves the remote two-gabled-window face or tests all four façade layouts. The exact real compass orientation, glazing and optic type, fine sash patterns, current paint, tides, stairs/handrail and entry landing dimensions remain unverified.

The actual 2022 site shows vegetation, an irregular, visibly stratified red cliff, talus and wet intertidal foreshore. The game retains simplified tan slopes and a harsh shoreline edge (including foreground occlusion in the entry view). No yard, stratigraphy or realistic coast claim.

The owner’s 14.3 m and chart-listed structure 14.4 m are documentary, with a conflicting historic 18.5 m listing. The photo comparisons do not resolve the discrepancy or measure the game/site; focal elevation above water is not building height.
